Characterize WGCNA modules through functional enrichment analysis

rna_wgcna_enrichment.Rd

Performs gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA) to characterize the biological processes and molecular functions associated with WGCNA co-expression modules.

Genes are ranked according to their signed module membership (kME), calculated as the correlation between gene expression and the corresponding module eigengene. Enrichment analysis is performed independently for each selected module using the fgseaMultilevel algorithm.

Gene sets can be retrieved automatically from MSigDB or supplied by the user as a named list or GMT file. Gene identifiers are mapped to the identifiers used in the original WGCNA network before enrichment analysis.

Usage

rna_wgcna_enrichment(
  project,
  modules = NULL,
  geneset_collection = "C5",
  geneset_subcollection = "GO:BP",
  pathways = NULL,
  pathway_id_type = "symbol",
  min_size = 10,
  max_size = 500,
  plot_top = 5,
  plot = TRUE,
  plot_dir = NULL,
  save = TRUE
)

Arguments

project

An rna_project object containing a previously constructed WGCNA network generated by rna_wgcna and the corresponding gene annotation.

modules

Optional character vector specifying the WGCNA module colors to analyze. If NULL, all assigned modules are analyzed. Unassigned genes (grey modules) are excluded. Defaults to NULL.

geneset_collection

Character string specifying the MSigDB collection to retrieve when pathways = NULL. Common options include "H" (Hallmark), "C2" (curated gene sets), "C5" (ontology gene sets), "C6" (oncogenic signatures), "C7" (immunologic signatures), and "C8" (cellular signatures). Defaults to "C5".

geneset_subcollection

Optional character string specifying the MSigDB subcollection. For example, "GO:BP" selects Gene Ontology Biological Process gene sets, while "CP:REACTOME" selects Reactome pathways. Some collections do not support subcollections. Defaults to "GO:BP".

pathways

Optional collection of custom gene sets, supplied either as a named list of gene identifiers or as a path to a GMT file. If NULL, gene sets are retrieved automatically from MSigDB according to geneset_collection and geneset_subcollection. Defaults to NULL.

pathway_id_type

Character string specifying the identifier type used in custom gene sets. Supported options are "gene_id", "symbol", and "entrez". This argument is ignored when MSigDB gene sets are retrieved automatically, as MSigDB gene symbols are used. Defaults to "symbol".

min_size

Integer specifying the minimum number of mapped genes required for a gene set to be included in the enrichment analysis. Defaults to 10.

max_size

Integer specifying the maximum number of mapped genes allowed for a gene set to be included in the enrichment analysis. Defaults to 500.

plot_top

Integer specifying the maximum number of enriched pathways to visualize for each module. Pathways are selected according to their module-specific adjusted p-values (padj_module), regardless of statistical significance. Defaults to 5.

plot

Logical. If TRUE, generates enrichment plots for the top pathways of each analyzed module using plotEnrichment. Defaults to TRUE.

plot_dir

Optional character string specifying the directory in which enrichment plots are saved as PDF files. The directory is created recursively if it does not exist. If NULL, plots are not saved to disk. Defaults to NULL.

save

Logical. If TRUE, attaches the analysis result to the project under analyses$wgcna_enrichment and invisibly returns the updated project. Otherwise, invisibly returns an object of class wgcna_enrichment_result. Defaults to TRUE.

Value

If save = TRUE, invisibly returns the updated rna_project object.

If save = FALSE, invisibly returns an object of class wgcna_enrichment_result, containing:

  • enrichment: combined GSEA results for all analyzed module-by-pathway combinations, including enrichment scores, normalized enrichment scores, p-values, and adjusted p-values.

    \item \code{kME}: matrix of gene-module membership correlations between
all network genes and module eigengenes.

\item \code{rankings}: named list containing the signed kME rankings used
for each analyzed module.

\item \code{gene_sets}: gene sets mapped to the identifiers used in the
original WGCNA network and retained after size filtering.

\item \code{pathway_mapping}: summary of original and mapped gene set
sizes, including pathway inclusion status.

\item \code{module_summary}: summary of the number of genes, tested
pathways, and significant enrichment results for each module.

\item \code{plots}: nested list containing the enrichment plots generated
for each module.

\item \code{parameters}: organism, gene set source, collection,
identifier type, module selection, filtering thresholds, correlation
method, and plotting configuration.

\item \code{data_summary}: summary of the number of genes, samples,
modules, gene sets, and enrichment tests.

\item \code{timestamp}: date and time of analysis.

Input requirements

The project must contain a valid WGCNA result generated by rna_wgcna. The original result must include:

  • An expression matrix with samples in rows and genes in columns.

  • A gene-module assignment table containing gene identifiers, module labels, and module colors.

  • Module eigengenes corresponding to the original expression matrix.

When custom gene sets or MSigDB gene sets use symbols or Entrez identifiers, gene annotation must contain the corresponding identifiers and their mapping to the gene identifiers used in the WGCNA network.

Gene sets are mapped to the original network identifiers before analysis. Only mapped genes belonging to the original WGCNA network are retained. Gene sets are subsequently filtered according to their mapped sizes.

Analysis

Enrichment analysis is performed independently for each selected module using the signed module membership (kME) as the ranking statistic.

kME is calculated as the correlation between each gene and the corresponding module eigengene, using the correlation method specified during the original WGCNA analysis.

For each module, genes are ranked in decreasing order of kME. The resulting rankings are analyzed using the multilevel GSEA algorithm implemented in fgseaMultilevel.

Two levels of multiple-testing correction are reported:

  • Module-specific FDR (padj_module): Benjamini-Hochberg adjusted p-values calculated independently within each module, considering all tested gene sets.

    \item \strong{Global FDR (\code{padj_global}):}
Benjamini-Hochberg adjusted p-values calculated across all
module-by-pathway enrichment tests combined.

Enrichment plots display the running enrichment score of selected gene sets along the ranked gene list. The top pathways are selected according to module-specific adjusted p-values, even when they do not reach the conventional significance threshold.

Interpretation

Enrichment results characterize the functional composition of WGCNA modules and identify biological processes whose genes are concentrated toward one end of the module membership ranking.

The normalized enrichment score (NES) reflects the direction and magnitude of gene set enrichment relative to the signed kME ranking. Its sign indicates the direction of enrichment along that ranking, which depends on the orientation of the corresponding module eigengene.

Importantly, positive or negative NES values do not directly indicate biological pathway activation or inhibition. They describe the relative position of gene set members within the kME ranking and should be interpreted in the context of module eigengene orientation and gene expression patterns.

Enrichment results describe functional associations within co-expression modules and do not establish causal relationships, biochemical pathway activity, or functional activation of individual genes or cellular processes.

The analysis is based on the original WGCNA network and does not perform differential expression analysis, module-trait association testing, differential enrichment between experimental groups, or independent network reconstruction.

Statistical significance should be interpreted considering both module-specific and global FDR values, gene set size, annotation coverage, and the biological context of the analyzed modules.

References

Subramanian A, Tamayo P, Mootha VK, et al. (2005). Gene set enrichment analysis: a knowledge-based approach for interpreting genome-wide expression profiles. Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, 102(43), 15545–15550. doi:10.1073/pnas.0506580102

Korotkevich G, Sukhov V, Budin N, et al. (2021). Fast gene set enrichment analysis. bioRxiv. doi:10.1101/060012

Langfelder P, Horvath S. (2008). WGCNA: an R package for weighted correlation network analysis. BMC Bioinformatics, 9, 559. doi:10.1186/1471-2105-9-559
